passages.heading: Risk factors
passages.text: • Significant subsequent events General facts on Nokia Financial statements Other information Significant subsequent events Nokia to operate with two primary operating segments Nokia announced on 19 November 2025, together with its new strategy, that it will reorganize its business into two primary operating segments to better align to customer needs and accelerate innovation as the AI supercycle increases demand for advanced connectivity. This reorganization took effect as of 1 January 2026. The reorganization recognizes Network Infrastructure as a growth segment, positioned to capitalize on the rapid, global AI and data center build-out while continuing to innovate for its telecommunications customer base. The segment consists of three business units Optical Networks, IP Networks and Fixed Networks and is led by David Heard. The new Mobile Infrastructure segment brings together Nokia’s Core Networks portfolio, Radio Networks portfolio and Technology Standards (formerly Nokia Technologies). It is positioned for core and radio network technology and services leadership to lead the industry to AI-native networks and 6G. The new segment brings together a portfolio whose value creation is founded on mobile communication technologies based on 3GPP standards with a strong cash flow position underpinned by IP licensing. It is led by Justin Hotard on an interim basis and consists of three business units Core Software, Radio Networks and Technology Standards. In addition, as part of its strategy work, Nokia identified several units which are not seen as core to the future of the company’s strategy. These units were moved into a dedicated operating segment called Portfolio Businesses while the company assesses the best value creating opportunity for them. The units moved were: ▪ Fixed Wireless Access CPE (previously in Fixed Networks in Network Infrastructure) ▪ Site Implementation and Outside Plant (previously in Fixed Networks in Network Infrastructure) ▪ Enterprise Campus Edge (previously in Cloud and Network Services) ▪ Microwave Radio (previously in Mobile Networks) 114 Nokia Annual Report on Form 20-F 2025 General facts on Nokia American Depositary Shares 115 Controls and procedures 115 Government regulation 116 Sales in United States-sanctioned countries 116 Taxation 117 Key ratios 120 Alternative performance measures 121 115 Nokia Annual Report on Form 20-F 2025 Contents Business overview Corporate governance Operating and financial review and prospects General facts on Nokia • American Depositary Shares • Controls and procedures Government regulation Sales in United States- sanctioned countries Taxation Key ratios Alternative performance measures Financial statements Other information American Depositary Shares Fees and charges ADS holders may have to pay the following service fees to the Depositary : Service Fees, USD Issuance of ADSs Up to 5 cents per ADS (1) Cancellation of ADSs Up to 5 cents per ADS (1) Distribution of cash dividends or other cash distributions Up to 2 cents per ADS Distribution of ADSs pursuant to (i) stock dividends, free stock distributions or (ii) exercises of rights to purchase additional ADSs Up to 5 cents per ADS

credit_strengths.text: Nokia's balance sheet carries net cash, with cash and short-term investments exceeding reported borrowings, and the indicative financial risk profile is Minimal. Gross leverage sits at the sector median, but net leverage is negative, placing the company in the strongest percentile of its Information Technology peer group on a net basis.

Operating cash flow remains substantial and covers reported borrowings comfortably, while the current ratio exceeds one and is close to the sector median. This liquidity buffer, combined with recurring IP licensing cash flows from Technology Standards, supports the Minimal indicative risk profile despite the earnings decline.

key_risks.text: Operating income fell sharply year over year, compressing the operating margin well below the sector median and reducing interest coverage to a level far weaker than peers. The reorganization into Network Infrastructure and Mobile Infrastructure, effective from the start of the following year, introduces execution risk while Portfolio Businesses are assessed for value-creating alternatives.

Cash uses are significant: acquisitions, dividends and buybacks absorbed most of operating cash flow, and capital expenditure is not separately tagged, so free cash flow and its coverage of debt cannot be verified. This data gap is material because shareholder returns and deal spending could erode the net cash position if operating cash flow weakens.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Reported borrowings declined over the past three years, and with cash exceeding debt, net leverage is negative. Interest coverage, while positive, is well below the sector median, so debt service depends on restoring operating income rather than on balance-sheet strength alone. No debt maturity schedule was disclosed, limiting refinancing visibility.

Operating cash flow covers reported borrowings by a comfortable margin, and the current ratio indicates adequate near-term liquidity. However, without capital expenditure data, free cash flow after investment cannot be confirmed, and the heavy call on cash from acquisitions and shareholder distributions could reduce the cushion available for debt service.

overall_credit_view.text: Nokia presents a strong balance sheet with net cash, declining borrowings and a Minimal indicative financial risk profile. The main credit concern is the sharp earnings decline and margin compression, which leaves interest coverage far below the sector median and makes the net cash position the primary support for credit quality.

Our forward view is that the reorganization and portfolio review could improve focus and cash generation, but execution risk is elevated and capital expenditure disclosure is missing. We would monitor operating income recovery, free cash flow after investment, and the balance between acquisitions, shareholder returns and debt reduction before considering a more constructive stance.

credit_strengths.text: 諾基亞的資產負債表持有淨現金，現金及短期投資超過呈報借款，而指示性財務風險狀況為極低。總槓桿處於行業中位數，但淨槓桿為負，使該公司以淨額基準計位列其資訊科技同業組別中最強百分位。
營運現金流仍然龐大，並能輕鬆覆蓋呈報借款，而流動比率超過一，並接近行業中位數。此流動性緩衝，加上來自技術標準的經常性知識產權授權現金流，支持極低的指示性風險狀況，儘管盈利下降。

key_risks.text: 營運收入按年大幅下降，將營運利潤率壓縮至遠低於行業中位數，並使利息覆蓋率降至遠弱於同業的水平。自下一年年初起生效的重組為網絡基礎設施及移動基礎設施，帶來執行風險，同時投資組合業務正被評估價值創造的替代方案。
現金用途重大：收購、股息及回購吸收了大部分營運現金流，而資本開支並未單獨標示，因此自由現金流及其對債務的覆蓋無法核實。此數據缺口屬重大，因為若營運現金流減弱，股東回報及交易支出可能侵蝕淨現金狀況。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 呈報借款在過去三年下降，且由於現金超過債務，淨槓桿為負。利息覆蓋率雖為正數，但遠低於行業中位數，因此債務償付取決於恢復營運收入，而非僅依賴資產負債表實力。並未披露債務到期時間表，限制了再融資可見度。
營運現金流以舒適的幅度覆蓋呈報借款，而流動比率顯示短期流動性充足。然而，在沒有資本開支數據的情況下，投資後自由現金流無法確認，而收購及股東分派對現金的沉重需求可能減少可用於債務償付的緩衝。

overall_credit_view.text: 諾基亞呈現強勁的資產負債表，持有淨現金、借款下降及極低的指示性財務風險狀況。主要信貸關注點是盈利大幅下降及利潤率壓縮，使利息覆蓋率遠低於行業中位數，並使淨現金狀況成為信貸質量的主要支撐。
我們的前瞻觀點是，重組及投資組合檢討可能改善專注度及現金產生，但執行風險偏高，且資本開支披露缺失。在考慮更建設性的立場之前，我們將監察營運收入恢復、投資後自由現金流，以及收購、股東回報與債務削減之間的平衡。
